sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that war is called "krav" from the term for closeness, and that the soul's battle with the animal soul during prayer requires the divine soul to clothe itself in the animal soul.

translations.translation: "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, for many were with me."
And the Baal HaGeulah explains in his maamar beginning with this phrase
(printed in his book Shaarei Teshuvah),
that the reason war is called by the term "krav," from the language of closeness (kiruv)
(even though war is the opposite of closeness),
is,
that the essence of war is that each of the two combatants wants to defeat the other and subdue him so that he will be included within him,
and in order to effect this, that he fights against him so that he will be included within him,
it is specifically through the closeness that he draws near to him,
"krav" from the language of closeness.
And similarly, in the war of the divine soul and the animal soul,
the main war is during the time of prayer
(the time of prayer is the time of battle),
so that in order for the service
(prayer)
of the divine soul to affect the animal soul so that it becomes included in the divine soul
[meaning that the animal soul will also have love of G-d,
"with all your heart, with both your inclinations"],
it is through the divine soul clothing itself in the animal soul,
that the contemplation of the divine soul is in such matters and in such a manner that the animal soul can also grasp them.
However, when prayer is from the aspect of the soul itself,
it does not affect the animal soul,
as explained in the maamar.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the refinement of the animal soul through the divine soul clothing itself is a matter of war, whereas "He redeemed my soul in peace" refers to redemption through the revelation of a supernal light that nullifies the animal soul's desires without war.

translations.translation: Now, the refinement of the animal soul through the divine soul clothing itself in the animal soul,
is a matter of war,
as above.
For the essence of war is,
that there is an opponent and one must fight with him.
And the matter of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is that the redemption of the divine soul from the exile of the animal soul is not in a manner of war,
but rather,
that through the revelation of a supernal light, the desires of the animal soul are nullified,
so that there is no need for war at all.
And as explained in many places,
and also in the aforementioned maamar,
regarding the refinement through engaging in Torah,
which is not in the way of war
(meaning that there is an opponent but one defeats him through war,
but rather)
that through the revelation of the light of Torah, it is the nullification of evil in its very essence.
And similarly in prayer,
that through the love that is beyond reason and intellect, from the aspect of Chayah and Yechidah, the desires of the animal soul are nullified,
and the redemption of the divine soul from the exile of the animal soul is in a manner of peace,
"He redeemed my soul in peace."
